texts: good. the telling, both named participants, the day and year terms and the past tense are all there, and "the year had been difficult" is correctly recorded as what Meren said rather than as a fact of the world. only "day 270" is stored as a plain day number the translator's calendar treats as a day-of-month — a translator-side limit, not a phrasing problem.
good. the loss event carries the village, a group of three lanterns, the cold snaps and Year 1, with nothing unstated added.

bad: "beyond the six drained lanterns" is silently dropped, so the parse asserts flat-out that the village lost no lantern at all to the wraith — the opposite of what you wrote, since those six are exactly the ones it did lose. The translator has no way to carry an NP exceptive like "beyond"/"apart from", so its only compliant alternative is to drop the whole claim. Say it as an exhaustive positive instead: "The village lost only the six drained lanterns to the wraith."
good. the recovery lands on the six-lantern group and also distributes to each lantern, so a lantern named later still inherits its own recovery.

bad: "nearly" is meant to cancel the event, but the parse asserts a real running-out, leaves it untensed so it reads as something that happens as a matter of course, and files "almost" against the verb in a slot that only accepts an adjective — none of it is usable. The translator only handles "almost/nearly" over an adjective, so state it as a near-state: "The feather store was nearly empty in the winter of Year 1."

good. Old Vesh's report is correctly sealed as something he said rather than asserted, and the sky-cat drought and the near-miss are both bound to their earlier mentions. note that "the near-miss" hangs on the previous sentence's event, so it will follow whatever that sentence becomes.

mixed: every part of the proposal is captured and correctly kept inside "proposed", but the recommendation force is lost — "proposed that a few stations burn" is recorded as a flat claim that they do burn — and the station group exists only inside the proposal, which is what leaves the next sentence with nothing to point back at. Add an explicit modal: "Old Vesh proposed that a few stations of the Cliff Path should burn extra mire-essence in early winter, in order to draw crowds of nightmoths."

bad: "the bright stations" points back at a group that exists only inside the previous sentence's proposal, so nothing connects the two, and both per-member rules (brightness here, burning there) range over a group no fact asserts and can therefore never fire — this is the passage's unfireable-rule flag. The recommendation force is lost again, and bare "sky-cats" fills the hunter slot of a specific, located hunt where a definite group is needed. Best fix is to carry both proposals in one sentence so the stations are introduced once: "Old Vesh proposed that a few bright stations of the Cliff Path should burn extra mire-essence in early winter, in order to draw crowds of nightmoths and to keep the sky-cats hunting on the Cliff Path." If you want to keep two sentences, restate the stations rather than pointing back: "Old Vesh proposed that the stations burning extra mire-essence should keep the sky-cats hunting on the Cliff Path."

mixed: the Council, the taking-under-consideration and the past tense are all there, but "the proposal" is minted as a brand-new thing with no link back to Old Vesh's two proposing events, so the parse never says which proposal was taken up. Anchor it to the proposer: "The Council took Old Vesh's proposal under consideration."
